findings.impact: The registered SQLite-intended component suite selects PostgreSQL whenever the inherited new URL is nonempty, then seeds User and mutates actual application/private schedule rows there. The Rust workspace component unit also writes persistence.ts/postgres.sql/sqlite.sql/binding.json/ordinary-persistence.ts into any inherited absolute existing output directory. Normal clean-env63/63 does not establish isolation. This breaks the stated disposable-only test boundary even though the dedicated PG wrapper correctly unsets/replaces the DB URL.
findings.required_correction: Add BOTH new environment names to tools/verify.py's removal list before ANY workspace/runtime subprocess. Keep output supplied only by the test-owned mkdtemp harness and DB URL supplied only by the disposable postgres.sh mode. Do not weaken source-error assertions, guards or policy.

Unchanged generated component tests still pass SQLite with DB URL absent and PG through the disposable wrapper, or explicitly reuse matching frozen component pins when only verifier sanitation changes.

product_assessment.assessment: Only finished delivery_model bindings drive hooks. Create uses exact selected entity plus selected identity under the complete write census. Patch compares callable.name.text directly with the descriptor's qualified path and checks the entity; it does not prepend owner or infer by suffix/job spelling/JSON. Supplied field comes from the checked descriptor. Static census remains a prerequisite, not proof of runtime atomicity.

Hooked create/patch enter a whole-mutation client.transaction savepoint even inside an existing source transaction. INSERT/UPDATE, original sent reset and private revision helper all remain inside it. A caller catching helper conflict/exhaustion sees the source INSERT or patch/sent reset rolled back, while surrounding disjoint work can commit. Helper's additional nested savepoint does not replace the whole-mutation one.
